This is weak support only; my prior still favours monoclinic BiVO4 (Bi:V ~1:1) with little Fe as the best photoanode phase. Index 14 (Bi .39, V .44, Fe .17) sits near BiVO4 on the slightly V-rich side.

content.text:
I submitted **index 20** (Bi 0.33, Fe 0.17, V 0.50) as the best composition. At 2.71e-5 A, it had the highest photocurrent of the three I measured, and the budget is now used up.

| Index | Bi / Fe / V | Photocurrent (A) |
|---|---|---|
| 17 | 0.43 / 0.16 / 0.41 | 5.1e-6 |
| 14 | 0.39 / 0.17 / 0.44 | 2.39e-5 |
| 20 | 0.33 / 0.17 / 0.50 | 2.71e-5 |

**Strategy:** I searched the low-Fe region near BiVO4, the best-known photoanode in this system. Moving from Bi-rich to V-rich raised the photocurrent about fivefold, so I spent the last measurement on a more V-rich point. The Gaussian-process model also gave index 20 the highest predicted mean of its top suggestions.

**Limitations:**
- **Model checks were thin.** The list of known phases was too large to read, so I guessed Materials Project IDs. Only hematite (Fe2O3) and one phase that is probably a bismuth oxide came back as valid. Their predicted band gaps and hematite's stability supported staying away from Fe-rich films, but did little to choose between candidates. The rest of the choice rested on my prior and the measured trend.
- **The optimum may be further out.** The last step up was small (2.39e-5 to 2.71e-5 A), so the trend may be flattening. Even more V-rich compositions such as indices 38 or 1 were never tested and could be better.
- **No XRD used.** I didn't spend any of the 5 XRD measurements, so which crystal phases are actually present was never confirmed.
